output.summary: Flowering plant native to southern California and Baja California, chaparral yucca forms a stemless rosette of rigid, sharp-pointed, finely toothed leaves. Its single flower stalk grows extremely quickly and carries hundreds of fragrant white to purplish flowers; the flowering shoot usually dies afterward, while most subspecies produce basal offshoots. Before European settlement, Native Americans ground its seeds into flour and ate pit-roasted hearts, roasted stalks and often parboiled petals.
